title: Single Chamber and Dual Chamber Permanent Cardiac Pacemakers

criteria.question: Does the chart document that the patient has bradycardia?
criteria.evidence_hint: ECG, rhythm strip, telemetry, Holter/event monitor report, electrophysiology/cardiology note documenting bradycardia.

criteria.text: The bradycardia is due to a transient or correctable cause
criteria.question: Is the bradycardia due to a transient or correctable cause?
criteria.evidence_hint: Cardiology assessment or pre-procedure documentation addressing reversible causes such as electrolyte abnormalities, medications or drugs, hypothermia, rate-slowing medications, or metabolic workup.

criteria.text: The bradycardia is symptomatic, with documented symptoms directly attributable to the bradycardia (for example syncope, near-syncope, dizziness, confusion, exercise intolerance, heart failure symptoms)
criteria.question: Does the chart document symptoms directly attributable to the bradycardia?
criteria.evidence_hint: History and physical, cardiology/electrophysiology note, monitoring correlation, or assessment linking symptoms such as syncope, near-syncope, dizziness, confusion, exercise intolerance, or heart failure symptoms to bradycardia.

criteria.text: Sinus node dysfunction (sick sinus syndrome, sinus bradycardia, sinus arrest, sinoatrial block, chronotropic incompetence)
criteria.question: Is the bradycardia due to sinus node dysfunction?
criteria.evidence_hint: Cardiology/electrophysiology diagnosis, ECG, rhythm monitoring report, stress testing for chronotropic incompetence, or problem list documenting sick sinus syndrome, sinus bradycardia, sinus arrest, sinoatrial block, or chronotropic incompetence.

criteria.question: Is the bradycardia due to second-degree or third-degree AV block?
criteria.evidence_hint: ECG, telemetry, Holter/event monitor report, electrophysiology report, or cardiology note documenting second-degree AV block or third-degree AV block.

notes: Effective for claims with dates of service on and after August 13, 2013, CMS covers single-chamber or dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers when ALL of the following are met.
Billing table lists these codes as Covered when criteria met.
Applies to Medicare Advantage plans, including UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage, which follow CMS National Coverage Determinations for cardiac pacemakers.

Reproduced for software testing from the published NCD and the UF Health Jacksonville compliance checklist of NCD 20.8.3 (10/22/2018); wording reconstructed, verify against cms.gov before clinical use.

This section addresses single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers. It does not address biventricular pacemakers, devices that stimulate more than two chambers, devices intended to treat tachyarrhythmias or cardiac dyssynchrony, cardiac resynchronization therapy, or self-contained pacemaker monitors.
Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Bradycardia due to reversible causes, such as electrolyte abnormalities, medications or drugs, and hypothermia.
Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Asymptomatic first-degree AV block.
Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Asymptomatic sinus bradycardia.
Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Asymptomatic sinoatrial block or sinus arrest.

Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Ineffective atrial contractions (such as chronic atrial fibrillation or flutter, or giant left atrium) without symptomatic bradycardia.

Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Asymptomatic second-degree AV block of Mobitz Type I, unless the QRS complexes are prolonged or electrophysiological studies demonstrate that the block is at or beyond the level of the His bundle.
Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Syncope of undetermined cause.
Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Bradycardia during sleep.

Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Right bundle branch block with left axis deviation (and other forms of fascicular or bundle branch blocks) without syncope or other symptoms of intermittent AV block.

Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Asymptomatic bradycardia in post-myocardial infarction patients about to initiate long-term beta-blocker drug therapy.

Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: Frequent or persistent supraventricular tachycardias, except where the pacemaker is specifically for the control of the tachycardia.

Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for: A clinical condition in which pacing takes place only intermittently and briefly, and which is not associated with a reasonable likelihood that pacing needs will become prolonged.

All other indications for single-chamber or dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers not otherwise indicated as covered or non-covered above remain at local Medicare Administrative Contractor discretion.

Billing table lists 33227–33229 and 33233, Pulse generator removal/replacement, as MAC discretion. The scope status enum has no MAC-discretion value; these codes are therefore listed as covered in scope only to retain every billing code, and they are not included in the national coverage scenario.
Diagnosis codes and modifier requirements are specified in Local Coverage Article A54926.

Documentation should include the rhythm diagnosis, the symptoms attributed to the bradycardia and their correlation with the rhythm, and the exclusion of reversible causes (including review of rate-slowing medications and metabolic workup).
